comment: Timekeeping policy for the S10+ (beyond2lte). Read by tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-time.sh (installed as `nuxelctl time`) and by the nuxel-rtc-check timer. Nothing here is applied by itself: the tool reads it, reports what the system actually does, and refuses to claim a PASS it cannot observe.

timesync.comment_mode: auto = use systemd-timesyncd if it is installed AND enabled; otherwise chrony if installed; otherwise report NO_TIMESYNC_BACKEND (never silently pretend NTP is running).

rtc.comment: The S10+ RTC lives in the Samsung PMIC. The exact driver/binding is NOT assumed: the tool enumerates /sys/class/rtc/* and reports the real name so the claim can be checked instead of guessed.

kernel.comment: Both are kernel-side requirements for RTC persistence and are verified from the running kernel, never assumed: CONFIG_RTC_HCTOSYS (set the system clock from the RTC at boot) and CONFIG_RTC_DRV_S5M-family (the PMIC RTC driver). /sys/class/rtc existing is the observable proof that a driver bound.

launcher.comment: The launcher clock is rendered from the bridge's phone-status payload (services/nuxel-bridge/src/api.py -> _get_system_phone_status, field "time", local HH:MM). Comparing that value with the system clock is what makes 'the launcher clock agrees with the system' an observable statement instead of a promise.

journal.comment: journald timestamps must agree with the system clock; a frozen journald after an RTC restore is a real failure mode and is checked directly.

reboot_persistence.comment: Owner-driven: `nuxelctl time mark` before the reboot, `nuxelctl time compare` after it. The verdict is computed from the two real RTC readings and a boot-id change, not from the fact that a reboot happened.
